stem: Which statement correctly compares the means and the standard deviations of the number of clinic visits for the two towns?
stimulus:
A public health team asked residents of two towns how many times each had visited a health clinic in the past year. The team surveyed 20 residents in Town A and 40 residents in Town B. The results are shown in the table.

Annual Clinic Visits per Resident
Number of visits | Town A frequency | Town B frequency
1 | 5 | 2
2 | 2 | 8
3 | 6 | 20
4 | 2 | 8
5 | 5 | 2
choices: The means are equal, and the standard deviation for Town A is greater.
The means are equal, and the standard deviation for Town B is greater.
The means are equal, and the standard deviations are equal.
The mean for Town B is greater, and the standard deviation for Town B is greater.
explanation: Both distributions are symmetric about 3 visits, so both means are 3. In Town A, 10 of the 20 residents are at the extremes (1 or 5 visits). In Town B, half of the 40 residents are exactly at the center and only 4 are at the extremes. Town A's data sit farther from the mean, so Town A has the greater standard deviation.

B.why: You reversed the relationship. Town B's values are packed around 3, which makes its standard deviation smaller, not larger. The bigger frequencies in Town B come from surveying more people, not from more spread.

C.why: You saw the same center and the same range (1 to 5) and decided the spreads were equal. Range ignores how many values sit far from the mean, and Town A has far more of its data at the extremes.

D.why: You treated Town B's larger frequencies as larger data values. The frequencies only count residents. The visit numbers are the same 1 through 5 in both towns, and both sets are centered at 3.

stem: Which list of calcium amounts has the smallest standard deviation?
stimulus: A nutrition science lab measured the calcium content, in milligrams (mg), of one serving of each of six fortified plant-based milks. The lab then repeated the measurements on three other groups of six products. Each list below shows one group's results, and every list has a mean of 400 mg.
explanation: Every list is centered at 400 mg. In choice C, four of the six values are exactly 400 and only two are 40 mg away. No other list has so much of its data at the mean. Its values are the most tightly clustered around the center, so it has the smallest standard deviation, even though its range is not the smallest.

A.why: You picked the list with the smallest range (60 mg) and the fewest distinct values. Every value in this list is 30 mg from the mean and none is at the center, so it is more spread out than choice C.

B.why: You saw that this list's range (70 mg) is smaller than choice C's (80 mg) and stopped there. Four of its values are 35 mg from the mean, while choice C has four values right at the mean, so choice C has less spread.

D.why: This list has the largest standard deviation, not the smallest: four of its values are 60 mg from the mean. You answered the opposite of what was asked.

stem: Which statement correctly compares the standard deviations of the two data sets?
stimulus:
An immunology study recorded the number of days after vaccination until antibodies were first detected in the blood of each volunteer. The results for two groups of 8 volunteers are listed.

Group A: 5, 6, 6, 7, 7, 7, 7, 11
Group B: 5, 9, 9, 9, 9, 10, 10, 11
choices: The standard deviation of Group A is greater.
The standard deviation of Group B is greater.
The standard deviation of Group B is 2 days greater.
The standard deviations of the two groups are equal.
explanation: Group A has a mean of 7 days, with deviations of −2, −1, −1, 0, 0, 0, 0, and 4. Group B has a mean of 9 days, with deviations of −4, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, and 2. These are the same distances from the center, just mirrored, so Group B is Group A flipped. Flipping a data set does not change how far its values are from the mean, so the standard deviations are equal.

A.why: You saw Group A's lone high value (11) stretching to the right and read that tail as extra spread. Group B has a matching tail on the low side (5), just as far from its mean.

B.why: You judged spread by the size of the values. Group B's numbers are larger and its mean is higher, but standard deviation measures distance from the mean, not where the data sit.

C.why: You subtracted the means (9 − 7 = 2) and reported that difference as a difference in standard deviations. The means differ by 2 days, but the spreads are identical.

stem: Which statement correctly compares the ranges and the standard deviations of the wind speeds at the two stations?
stimulus:
A meteorologist recorded the wind speed, in miles per hour (mph), at noon on each of 20 days at two weather stations. The mean wind speed at each station was 13 mph.

Noon Wind Speeds
Wind speed (mph) | Station P frequency | Station Q frequency
10 | 1 | 0
11 | 1 | 10
12 | 2 | 0
13 | 12 | 0
14 | 2 | 0
15 | 1 | 10
16 | 1 | 0
choices: Station P has the greater range and the greater standard deviation.
Station P has the greater range, and Station Q has the greater standard deviation.
Station Q has the greater range and the greater standard deviation.
Station Q has the greater range, and Station P has the greater standard deviation.
explanation: Station P's range is 16 − 10 = 6 mph, and Station Q's is 15 − 11 = 4 mph, so P has the greater range. For spread, 12 of Station P's 20 days were exactly at the mean of 13 mph. Every one of Station Q's days was 2 mph from the mean. Station Q's data sit farther from the center overall, so Station Q has the greater standard deviation.

A.why: You assumed the larger range and the larger number of distinct speeds meant a larger standard deviation. Most of Station P's days are bunched at 13 mph, so its standard deviation is the smaller one.

C.why: You got the standard deviation right but reversed the range. Station Q's speeds only run from 11 to 15 mph, a range of 4, while Station P's run from 10 to 16, a range of 6.

D.why: You reversed both comparisons. Station P has the wider range, and Station Q, with every value 2 mph from the mean, has the larger standard deviation.

stem: Which list of verse counts has the largest standard deviation?
stimulus: A folklore studies researcher collected versions of a traditional ballad from four regions. Each list below gives the number of verses in six versions from one region. Every list has a mean of 12 verses.
explanation: All four lists are centered at 12. In choice A, every value is 4 verses from the mean. In choice B, four values sit right at the mean and only two are 6 away, so choice A's data are farther from the center overall. Choices C and D are packed even closer to 12. Choice A has the largest standard deviation, even though its range is not the largest.

B.why: You picked the list with the largest range (12 verses). Four of its six values equal the mean exactly, so its data sit closer to the center than choice A's, where no value is at the mean.

C.why: You judged spread by the number of distinct values. This list has six different values, but each one is only 1 to 3 verses from the mean.

D.why: This list has the smallest standard deviation: two values are at the mean and the rest are only 2 away. You answered the opposite of what was asked.

stem: Which statement correctly compares the means and the standard deviations of the jump heights for the two groups?
stimulus:
A sports science study measured the vertical jump height, in centimeters (cm), of 20 athletes in Group X and 20 athletes in Group Y. The results are shown in the table.

Vertical Jump Heights
Jump height (cm) | Group X frequency | Group Y frequency
40 | 2 | 0
45 | 5 | 2
50 | 6 | 5
55 | 5 | 6
60 | 2 | 5
65 | 0 | 2
choices: The mean for Group Y is greater, and the standard deviation for Group Y is greater.
The means are equal, and the standard deviations are equal.
The mean for Group X is greater, and the standard deviations are equal.
The mean for Group Y is greater, and the standard deviations are equal.
explanation: Group Y's frequencies (2, 5, 6, 5, 2) are Group X's frequencies moved up one row, so every Group Y height is 5 cm higher. That raises the mean from 50 cm to 55 cm. The shape is identical, though, so each value is the same distance from its own mean, and the standard deviations are equal.

A.why: You saw that Group Y's data sit higher and assumed they were more spread out too. Moving every value up by 5 cm moves the center but does not change the distances from it.

B.why: You compared the frequency patterns, which are identical, and missed that Group Y's pattern starts at 45 cm instead of 40 cm. The shapes match, but the centers do not.

C.why: You saw that the spreads match and the centers differ, but you got the direction wrong. Group Y's heights are the higher ones, so Group Y has the greater mean.

stem: Which statement correctly orders the standard deviations of the skein weights for the three spinners, from smallest to largest?
stimulus:
A textile history museum weighed 10 hand-spun wool skeins made by each of three 19th-century spinners, X, Y, and Z, using period tools. Each spinner's skeins have a mean weight of 50 grams (g).

Skein Weights
Weight (g) | Spinner X frequency | Spinner Y frequency | Spinner Z frequency
48 | 1 | 2 | 4
49 | 2 | 2 | 1
50 | 4 | 2 | 0
51 | 2 | 2 | 1
52 | 1 | 2 | 4
choices: Spinner Z, Spinner Y, Spinner X
Spinner Y, Spinner X, Spinner Z
Spinner X, Spinner Y, Spinner Z
All three standard deviations are equal.
explanation: All three spinners have the same mean (50 g) and the same range (48 to 52 g). Spinner X has most of its skeins at or next to 50 g, so it has the least spread. Spinner Y's skeins are spread evenly across all five weights. Spinner Z has 8 of its 10 skeins at the extremes. From smallest to largest standard deviation, the order is X, Y, Z.

A.why: You put the spinners in order from largest to smallest standard deviation. Spinner Z, with most skeins at 48 g and 52 g, has the most spread, not the least.

B.why: You read Spinner Y's flat, even distribution as the tightest because no weight stands out. Spinner X has 4 skeins right at the mean, while Spinner Y has 4 skeins at the extremes, so Spinner X is the more tightly clustered.

D.why: You saw the shared mean and the shared range and stopped there. The spinners put very different numbers of skeins far from 50 g, and that is what standard deviation measures.

stem: Which of the following lists of dive durations has a smaller standard deviation than the list recorded for the tagged dolphin?
stimulus: A marine biologist tagged a bottlenose dolphin and recorded the duration, in seconds, of five of its dives: 20, 25, 30, 35, and 40.
explanation: The tagged dolphin's dives are centered at 30 seconds, with values 0, 5, and 10 seconds from the mean. In choice B, three values sit at 30 and the other two are only 5 seconds away. Those values are packed more tightly around the center than the original list, so choice B has the smaller standard deviation.

A.why: You noticed three values at the mean and stopped there. The other two values are 20 seconds from the mean, much farther than anything in the original list, so this list's standard deviation is larger.

C.why: This list is the original with 100 seconds added to every dive. It is the same shape at a different location, so its standard deviation is equal to the original, not smaller.

D.why: You saw the same range (20 to 40) and assumed the spread was the same or smaller. Here four of the five values are 10 seconds from the mean, so the data are more spread out than the original.
